:::{#exr-slr-mean-dot-product}
#### Mean as a dot product

Show that in simple linear regression (@def-slr),
the conditional mean $\mean(x_i)$ is the dot product
of the covariate vector $\vxi$ (@def-slr-covariate-vector)
and the coefficient vector $\vcoef = \tp{\paren{\intcoef, \coef{x}}}$ (@exm-normal-equations-slr):
$\mean(x_i) = \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}$.
:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#sol-slr-mean-dot-product}

Start from the dot product:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}
&= \dprod{\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ x_i \end{pmatrix}}{\vcoef}
&& \text{(definition of $\vxi$)}\\
&= \dprod{\begin{pmatrix} 1 \\ x_i \end{pmatrix}}{\begin{pmatrix} \intcoef \\ \coef{x} \end{pmatrix}}
&& \text{(definition of $\vcoef$, written as a column)}\\
&= 1 \cdot \intcoef + x_i \coef{x}
&& \text{(definition of the dot product)}\\
&= \intcoef + x_i \coef{x}
&& \text{($1 \cdot a = a$)}\\
&= \intcoef + \coef{x} x_i
&& \text{(reorder the factors)}\\
&= \mean(x_i)
&& \text{(definition of $\mean(x)$)}
\end{aligned}
$$

So $\mean(x_i) = \dprod{\vxi}{\vcoef}$.

:::
